A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MambaVO/MambaVO++ work, with readable text, equations, tables and figures. V1 includes Appendices A–B; v2 ends after the references, allowing the appendix omissions to be established.

before.justification: V1 reports original pose-estimation, matching, ablation and memory results, plus appendix matching, trajectory and map visualizations.

after.justification: V2 retains the original benchmark and ablation results and additionally reports dataset-specific inference rates in Section 5.4.

M1.justification: The GIM, GMM, TAP losses, bundle adjustment and loop-closure procedures remain unchanged. V2 clarifies temporal nearest-keyframe selection and initialization of the first history token from GIM features; these are additional implementation descriptions, without evidence of a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions train on TartanAir and evaluate monocular odometry/SLAM on TartanAir, EuRoC, KITTI and TUM-RGBD. The omitted appendix visualizations concern datasets and sequences still represented in the retained evaluations.

E2.justification: The separate visual comparison against DPVO in Appendix B.1/Figure 8 is removed. Comparator membership in all seven tables and the GPU-memory comparison remains unchanged, including DPVO's participation in the quantitative comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 5 changes the reported training GPU from one RTX 3090 to one RTX 4090. Training remains 196k steps with batch size 1, and the stated splits, metrics, monocular setting and loop-closure grouping are unchanged. This establishes a reported hardware-setting revision, without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 removes Appendix B.1's qualitative diagnostic of matching accuracy and spatial distribution against DPVO, along with the selected trajectory case studies in Appendix B.2. The controlled feature-selection, component and loss-smoothing ablations in Tables 6–7 and Figure 5 remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions state that evaluations are run five times and report mean ATE. Neither adds confidence intervals, significance tests, seed details or another uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: V2 newly reports MambaVO inference rates of 22 Hz on EuRoC, 30 Hz on TUM-RGBD and 23 Hz on KITTI; v1 only states real-time operation. Appendix matching, trajectory and map results, including per-trajectory numerical annotations, disappear. All seven tables retain identical numerical entries, and the main training curves and memory results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The graph formulation, projection relationships, refinement equations, bundle-adjustment objective and training losses in Equations 1–15 are mathematically unchanged. Neither version supplies additional theorems or proofs, including in v1's appendix.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain robust initialization, Mamba-based sequential matching refinement, TAP training smoothing and the loop-closure extension. Claims of state-of-the-art accuracy, real-time operation and reduced GPU memory remain in the introduction despite the shortened abstract.

C2.justification: V2 deletes the conclusion's explicit limitation that MambaVO produces only sparse maps because it uses semi-dense matching pixels. Appendix interpretations concerning matching distribution and performance under challenging motions and long trajectories also disappear. The main explanations of component benefits remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Deleting Appendix A removes important reproduction details: 100 randomly selected matches per frame, the DINO-v2 small model with registers, patch-to-pixel deconvolution, three Mamba blocks and chronological token ordering. V2 adds the first-history-token initialization detail and revises the reported training GPU, but does not restore those specifications. It also removes the promise to release code; neither PDF establishes actual code availability.

R1.justification: V2 adds four cited works: RoCo, GSLAMOT, a UAV relative-state-estimation paper and a multi-robot localization survey. These expand introductory citations without substantially changing the related-work discussion or the claimed novelty of applying state-space models to visual odometry.

P1.justification: The main section order and most wording persist. Changes include shortening the abstract and introductory repetition, updating affiliations, adding brief implementation clarifications and correcting the GMM figure reference from Figure 7 to Figure 3. Appendices A–B are omitted rather than integrated into the main narrative.

P2.justification: V2 removes Figures 7–11: the detailed Mamba-block diagram, DPVO matching comparison, supplementary trajectory panels and sparse-map visualizations. Retained figures and tables are redistributed across pages, and all tables now precede the references instead of some interrupting the bibliography. This substantially changes the visual material available to readers.

improvement.justification: V2 usefully quantifies inference speed, clarifies history initialization and improves table placement. However, removing Appendix A makes the implementation harder to reproduce, while deleting qualitative evidence and the explicit sparse-map limitation reduces transparency. These losses outweigh the limited additions, although the unchanged method, benchmark tables and controlled ablations preserve the paper's central scientific content.
